{"id": "5087402d-34ba-4a28-9b0e-7b3b7638c98d", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Classic cold start behavior. A quick explanation of what's happening, then I can check your specific functions if you want to pin down why it's happening to you.

**What causes it:**
- Lambda tears down execution environments that go idle for a while (roughly 15–60+ min of no invocations, though exact timing isn't published/guaranteed)
- The next request after that has to spin up a brand new environment: download the code package, start the runtime, run any init code (SDK clients, DB connections, config loads) — all before your handler code even runs
- This "init" overhead is the cold start; it's added on top of normal execution time only for that first request

**What commonly makes it worse:**
- Larger deployment packages or container images (more to download/unpack)
- VPC-attached functions (ENI setup used to be the big culprit; it's much faster now but still adds some latency)
- Heavy initialization code — large SDK imports, DB/connection pool setup, loading big dependencies
- Lower memory allocation (CPU scales with memory, so init code runs slower)
- Runtime choice — Java/.NET typically cold-start slower than Python/Node/Go

**What fixes it:**
- Provisioned Concurrency — keeps warm environments ready, eliminates cold starts for that concurrency level
- Reduce package size, lazy-load non-critical dependencies
- Bump memory (also increases CPU)
- Move SDK client/connection setup outside the handler so it's reused across warm invocations

Want me to pull up the actual configs for your eu-central-1 functions — memory, runtime, VPC attachment, package size, provisioned concurrency settings — so we can see which of these is actually in play for you?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
